παρέκοψε τὸ »λέγετε ὅτι ἀχρεῖοι δοῦλοί ἐσμεν· ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν«.

records.reason: Faith like a mustard seed (17:5–6) and the servant who does what he is told (17:7–10): two NA27 paragraphs with no attested present verse (METHOD §4.3). Epiphanius states that the text lacked 17:10b ("say, we are unworthy servants; we have done what we ought to have done"), which is A− (NA27: □ McionE). Tertullian passes from 17:4 (4.35.3) to 17:14 (4.35.4).

witnesses.evidence: "In Samariae regionibus res agebatur, unde erat et unus interim ex leprosis."

ὅτε συνήντησαν οἱ δέκα λεπροί. ἀπέκοψε δὲ πολλὰ καὶ ἐποίησεν »ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς λέγων, δείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσι« καὶ ἄλλα ἀντὶ ἄλλων ἐποίησε, λέγων ὅτι »πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν ἡμέραις Ἐλισσαίου τοῦ προφήτου καὶ οὐκ ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Νεεμὰν ὁ Σύρος«.
"in curatione decem leprosorum".

records.wording: NA27, including its bracketed [αὐτῷ] (SBLGNT omits it — checked on the page image), without the clause "who stood at a distance" (οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν). Epiphanius says that after "when the ten lepers met him" Marcion "cut out much" and put "other things in place of others", quoting 4:27. Roth takes the omitted "much" to be 17:12b–13, the lepers standing at a distance and crying "Jesus, master, have mercy on us", and 4:27 as what stood in its place. Tertullian's account of the healing has neither.

witnesses.evidence: ὅτε συνήντησαν οἱ δέκα λεπροί. ἀπέκοψε δὲ πολλὰ καὶ ἐποίησεν »ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς λέγων, δείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσι« καὶ ἄλλα ἀντὶ ἄλλων ἐποίησε, λέγων ὅτι »πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν ἡμέραις Ἐλισσαίου τοῦ προφήτου καὶ οὐκ ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Νεεμὰν ὁ Σύρος«.

records.reason: "And they raised their voices, saying, Jesus, master, have mercy on us." Part of what Epiphanius says Marcion "cut out" between the meeting with the ten lepers and the command to the priests; Roth: not present (with 17:12b). Tertullian stresses that they were healed "without touch and without a word" from Jesus, and does not mention their plea.

records.wording: NA27. Epiphanius' "he sent them away saying" is probably his own introduction (Roth). His δείξατε for ἐπιδείξατε is rated possible only.

witnesses.evidence: "quia satis iam obtulerat gloriam deo reddens".
"Et ideo, Fides tua te salvum fecit, audiit".
"Sed nec pharisaei possunt videri de alterius dei regno consuluisse dominum quando venturum sit… Non venit, inquit, regnum dei cum observatione".
"nec dicunt, Ecce hic, ecce illic: ecce enim regnum dei intra vos est."

records.wording: Marcionite reading adopted: the second "Look" (ἰδού) before "there" (Tertullian's "ecce… ecce"; Roth: very likely). The Greek printed is that of A D W Θ Ψ and the Byzantine text (NA27 apparatus: ἢ ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ); NA27 prints "Look, here!" or "There!".

witnesses.evidence: »ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι, ὅταν ἐπιθυμήσητε ἰδεῖν μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου«.

records.wording: NA27. Epiphanius has ὅταν and the verb ἰδεῖν before "one of the days"; Roth: order uncertain.
